findings.claim: The corrected diagnostic string (trailing period dropped before the wrapped-error colon) is not asserted by any test in the package; every existing assertion touching this message only checks for substring presence of the word nextRecommended, which passes whether or not the original punctuation collision is present, so a regression reintroducing the collision would go undetected.

evidence: engine/skills/load.go and engine/skills/load_test.go are pure deletions. An exhaustive text search for the identifier across every .go file in the candidate tree's Go modules (engine's ~40 source and test files spanning skills, cmd, gate, runtime, settings, propagator, prespec, gadu, installer, assets; tui's 9 files; and all three tools/* modules) found zero remaining call sites of the deleted Load(path string) function. Every remaining textual match for 'Load' resolves to unrelated, still-present functions (LoadManifestView in the skills package, LoadContractPhases in the runtime package) — the deletion took nothing live with it.

ParseRegistry (unchanged, defined outside the manifest in the same package as the deleted files) remains called from at least six production call sites in that package and is exercised by a pre-existing, independent table-driven test suite covering valid and malformed inputs via real on-disk fixtures, plus separate production-path tests elsewhere in the same package that independently cover a missing-registry-file error and a malformed-registry-YAML parse error through the injected readFile mechanism used by production entry points. None of that coverage depended on the deleted load_test.go, so the deletion drops no proof of ParseRegistry's behavior or its error handling.

engine/skills/skills_test.go: RenderValidateCore (defined outside the manifest) passes the --source-root flag value through to scanSkills completely unmodified — no filepath.Abs or cwd-relative resolution is applied to it. That makes the new recording-stub assertion (recorded scanned directory equals the exact expected --source-root value) a genuine, non-vacuous check: it would fail today if production stopped honoring --source-root, e.g. by resolving it against the working directory or falling back to it. Each of the four table-driven subtests builds its own fresh recording stub inside its own t.Run closure (no shared mutable state across subtests) and calls os.Chdir(tt.cwd) itself immediately before invoking RenderValidateCore, so per-subtest correctness does not depend on execution order. The one piece of shared state — os.Chdir to a candidate cwd with restoration only via a single t.Cleanup registered once, before the subtest loop, on the outer test — is carried over unchanged from the prior version of this test (which also chdir'd in a loop with a single deferred restore) and is not a new risk introduced by this diff; none of the affected tests call t.Parallel, so Go's -shuffle flag (which does not reorder subtests dynamically registered via sequential t.Run calls in a running goroutine) cannot interleave them unexpectedly.
